lessons.name: IEEE ICRA 2026 (Vienna) and its competitions
lessons.summary: ICRA 2026 was IEEE's robotics research conference in Vienna, with competitions that tested robots on concrete tasks.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

ICRA 2026 was IEEE's robotics research conference in Vienna, with competitions that tested robots on concrete tasks.

![Official ICRA 2026 conference logo](/img/lessons/orgs_event_2-ieee-icra-2026-vienna-and-its-competitions.webp)
*Official ICRA 2026 conference logo. Source: [Publisher](https://2026.ieee-icra.org/), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Research and demonstrations:** The Vienna edition ran on 1–5 June 2026 at VIECON / Messe Wien, alongside a dedicated competition area.
- **Nine challenges:** Examples included robotic grasping, RoboRacer racing, garment manipulation in LeHome, and legged robots moving over difficult terrain.
- **Software analogy:** Think of each challenge as an integration-test suite: a full robot must complete the task, not merely run one clever function.

> **Key idea:** A competition turns a broad research topic into a task with observable successes and failures.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Pick a tractable slice:** LeHome's garment task gives a concrete reason to study perception and learning, rather than starting with an unrestricted household robot.
- **Read across events:** Compare the research focus with RoboCup German Open, where teams also expose complete systems to shared competition conditions.
- **Worked exercise:** Choose one challenge and write a table of inputs, allowed actions, success conditions, and failure cases before attempting its baseline.

## How to engage

1. **Use the archive:** Watch a conference presentation, then follow the competition directory to that challenge's own technical rules.
2. **Reproduce first:** Run an available baseline and save its configuration, logs, and failed trials before proposing an improvement.
3. **Check the edition:** The Vienna competition has ended; use its materials for learning, not as a current registration invitation.

lessons.name: iREX (International Robot Exhibition)
lessons.summary: iREX is a Japanese exhibition where robot makers show industrial machines, service robots, and the components that make them work.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

iREX is a Japanese exhibition where robot makers show industrial machines, service robots, and the components that make them work.

![Franka Robotics' published preview of its iREX 2025 demonstration](/img/lessons/orgs_event_2-irex-international-robot-exhibition.webp)
*Franka Robotics' published preview of its iREX 2025 demonstration. Source: [Publisher](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CvJvWE6kQAw), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Three useful categories:** The official site separates Smart Production Robot, Smart Community Robot, and Component Technologies.
- **Production versus service:** Welding and picking appear alongside cleaning, delivery, and nursing applications; the show is broader than humanoid demonstrations.
- **Software analogy:** Picture a package ecosystem made physical: complete robots are applications, while drives, sensors, and control systems are dependencies.

> **Key idea:** A robot exhibition is most useful when you trace a complete application back to its enabling components.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **See the whole stack:** A software team can inspect how an arm, its tool, sensing, and application fit together rather than treating hardware as a black box.
- **Worked comparison:** Watch Franka Robotics and Agile Robots' 2025 booth videos; list what each demonstration senses, moves, and handles.
- **Compare regions:** ROBOTWORLD offers another Asian exhibition viewpoint, while LogiMAT narrows the focus to warehouse and material-flow applications.

## How to engage

1. **Start remotely:** Use the exhibitor directory to pick a specific application, then read the maker's supporting technical material.
2. **Ask concrete questions:** Request interface documentation and operating constraints for the demonstrated task, not a vague promise that a robot supports AI.
3. **Check names carefully:** The site announces iREX for early December 2027; RoboNext 2026 is a separate event, not the next iREX edition.

lessons.name: KUKA Innovation Award
lessons.summary: The KUKA Innovation Award is a robotics competition that helps selected teams turn research ideas into demonstrations using KUKA equipment.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

The KUKA Innovation Award is a robotics competition that helps selected teams turn research ideas into demonstrations using KUKA equipment.

![KUKA Innovation Award trophies](/img/lessons/orgs_event_2-kuka-innovation-award.webp)
*KUKA Innovation Award trophies. Source: [Publisher](https://www.kuka.com/en-de/future-production/research-and-development/kuka-innovation-award), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Research-to-industry competition:** Developers, graduates, and research teams from universities or companies submit ideas addressing a task set by KUKA.
- **Support for finalists:** KUKA lists a supplied robot, training, coaching, and a trade-fair presentation; the winning team receives €20,000.
- **Changing brief:** The 2026 Circular Packaging Challenge concerned packaging's life cycle, including putting products into packaging and recovering packaging for recycling.

> **Key idea:** The valuable constraint is solving a specified application, not simply making an industrial arm move.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Software analogy:** Treat the call like an API contract: an impressive implementation still fails if it does not satisfy the requested behavior.
- **Worked exercise:** Turn one circular-packaging operation into a proposal with an input object, robot action, measurable outcome, and recovery strategy.
- **Prepare progressively:** WorldSkills France offers a complementary view of robot integration: programming is only one part of making an industrial process work.

## How to engage

1. **Read the current call:** Confirm the theme, eligibility, and application process instead of reusing requirements from an older award video.
2. **Study previous finalists:** Identify the problem, robot setup, and evidence each team presented, then compare them with your proposed contribution.
3. **Scope before applying:** Explain what the student team can already demonstrate and which equipment or coaching it would need to complete the application.

lessons.name: LauzHack
lessons.summary: LauzHack is a student-run EPFL hackathon for building team prototypes, not a robotics-only competition.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

LauzHack is a student-run EPFL hackathon for building team prototypes, not a robotics-only competition.

![Published preview of LauzHack 2025](/img/lessons/orgs_event_2-lauzhack.webp)
*Published preview of LauzHack 2025. Source: [Publisher](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=j1CmyWgrC18), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Build a demonstration:** LauzHack describes hackathons as creativity and prototyping marathons where teams combine existing libraries and interfaces to show an idea.
- **Lausanne setting:** The 2026 edition is scheduled for 21–22 November at EPFL; the official page says applications are closed.
- **Software analogy:** This is closer to shipping a small vertical slice than finishing a production system: demonstrate the essential behavior end to end.

> **Key idea:** A short hackathon rewards a narrow, understandable prototype more than an ambitious robot you cannot demonstrate.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Practice team delivery:** Software students can rehearse the workflow of choosing a problem, integrating tools, and explaining what actually works.
- **Worked project pitch:** Propose a simulated robot sorting objects, with a visible input, decision, and outcome; ask organizers whether it fits the rules.
- **Choose the right venue:** Compare with LeRobot Worldwide Hackathon, whose published challenge materials explicitly focus on robotics and robot-learning demonstrations.

## How to engage

1. **Inspect an archive:** Watch the 2025 event video and read that edition's page to understand the format without confusing past and current arrangements.
2. **Read participation rules:** Check eligibility, team conditions, and what work can be prepared before a future edition.
3. **Ask before transporting hardware:** Confirm whether your proposed robot or simulation is suitable, and do not treat a closed application page as admission.

lessons.name: LeRobot Worldwide Hackathon
lessons.summary: LeRobot Worldwide Hackathon brought online and local teams together to build and share open-source robot-learning demonstrations.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

LeRobot Worldwide Hackathon brought online and local teams together to build and share open-source robot-learning demonstrations.

![Participants at the Paris LeRobot hackathon](/img/lessons/orgs_event_2-lerobot-worldwide-hackathon.webp)
*Participants at the Paris LeRobot hackathon. Source: [Publisher](https://42-ai.github.io/posts/LeRobotHackathonHighlights/), CC BY 4.0.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Distributed event:** The published hackathon ran on 14–15 June 2025, with online participation and local sites, including 42 Paris.
- **Shared artifacts:** Submission instructions asked teams for a demonstration video under one minute and the datasets they recorded, when relevant.
- **Robot-learning workflow:** The event introduced the SO-101 and linked LeRobot documentation for recording data and building working demonstrations.

> **Key idea:** A convincing hackathon submission pairs visible robot behavior with the data and code needed to understand it.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Direct local connection:** 42AI's announcement identifies 42, 96 Boulevard Bessières, as the Paris site; this is an existing community link, not a speculative introduction.
- **Software analogy:** Treat the demo as a release and its dataset as a versioned test fixture; both matter when another team investigates the behavior.
- **Worked submission:** Follow the published pattern `[TEAM-N°]-[TEAM NAME]-[DATASET-NAME]` when studying how event datasets were organized.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the kickoff:** Then browse the event organization and the Paris highlights to connect instructions with actual student work.
2. **Reproduce a small task:** With SO-101 and LeRobot, choose one observable behavior before extending it with more ambitious learning.
3. **Use current channels:** Follow official community updates for future opportunities; the June 2025 registration instructions describe an event that has already ended.

lessons.name: LogiMAT
lessons.summary: LogiMAT is a Stuttgart trade fair about moving, storing, and managing goods inside businesses, including warehouse robotics and automation.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

LogiMAT is a Stuttgart trade fair about moving, storing, and managing goods inside businesses, including warehouse robotics and automation.

![Exhibition floor at LogiMAT](/img/lessons/orgs_event_2-logimat.webp)
*Exhibition floor at LogiMAT. Source: [Publisher](https://www.logimat-messe.de/en), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Intralogistics:** This means material and information flow inside an organization, from receiving goods through storage, production, and distribution.
- **Process-level view:** The fair connects equipment with software and data handling; it is not a competition to build a single robot.
- **Concrete setting:** The official site advertises 16–18 March 2027 at Stuttgart Trade Fair Centre, with the theme Mind Meets Machine.

> **Key idea:** Warehouse robots only create value when their physical movements fit the surrounding information and material flow.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Software analogy:** Think of a warehouse as a distributed application: moving a box is one operation inside a larger workflow with state and interfaces.
- **Worked visit plan:** Trace one item's route from receipt to dispatch; record where sensing, transport, storage, and software handoffs occur.
- **Compare event scopes:** Robotics & Automation UK (with IntraLogisteX) is another application-focused route into warehouse automation rather than general robotics research.

## How to engage

1. **Learn the vocabulary:** Read the fair profile before watching the machine-vision forum, so its logistics examples have a clear context.
2. **Prepare an interface question:** Ask how a demonstrated solution receives tasks and reports exceptions; distinguish a polished booth sequence from an explained deployment.
3. **Check attendance conditions:** Use the organizer's current dates and visitor information before planning travel; remote talks are a useful first pass.

lessons.name: MACHINA (Station F physical-AI summit)
lessons.summary: MACHINA is a Paris summit about physical AI: applying artificial intelligence to robots and other machines that act in the world.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

MACHINA is a Paris summit about physical AI: applying artificial intelligence to robots and other machines that act in the world.

![Humanoid robot demonstration at MACHINA 2026](/img/lessons/orgs_event_2-machina-station-f-physical-ai-summit.webp)
*Humanoid robot demonstration at MACHINA 2026. Source: [Publisher](https://machinasummit.com/), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Beyond chat interfaces:** Discussions concern robot intelligence, deployment, and the infrastructure needed to move from prototypes to real applications.
- **Named speakers:** The official 2026 archive includes NVIDIA's Jim Fan and leaders from Google DeepMind, Apptronik, and Hugging Face.
- **Edition distinction:** The inaugural Station F event was in 2026; the current site advertises 7–8 July 2027 at Palais des Congrès.

> **Key idea:** Use a robotics summit to identify testable technical ideas, not to treat every stage prediction as a demonstrated capability.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Software analogy:** A summit is like a technology design review, not an executable benchmark: you still need to inspect the implementation and evidence.
- **Worked listening exercise:** Watch Jim Fan's session and separate three columns: capabilities shown, claims made, and experiments your lab could reproduce.
- **Connect formats:** Mistral AI Robotics Hackathon offers a contrasting hands-on format, where teams must build and pitch a working physical-AI demonstration.

## How to engage

1. **Start with recordings:** Watch the 2026 aftermovie for context, then a technical session before deciding whether the audience matches your goals.
2. **Prepare a precise introduction:** Bring one demonstrated task, a repository, and a concrete technical question rather than requesting an unspecified partnership.
3. **Check current access:** Consult official tickets and program pages; do not assume a summit pass includes a hackathon or robot workshop.

lessons.name: Mistral AI Robotics Hackathon
lessons.summary: Mistral AI Robotics Hackathon was a Paris event combining a physical-AI summit with a 48-hour robot-building sprint.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Mistral AI Robotics Hackathon was a Paris event combining a physical-AI summit with a 48-hour robot-building sprint.

![Published preview of the Mistral AI Robotics and Physical AI Hackathon](/img/lessons/orgs_event_2-mistral-ai-robotics-hackathon.webp)
*Published preview of the Mistral AI Robotics and Physical AI Hackathon. Source: [Publisher](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-oA0K_rTBKs), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Specific format:** The published April 11–13 event included a Friday summit and a weekend hackathon, followed by demonstrations and jury pitches.
- **Robot access:** The announcement offered more than 40 robotic arms from Hugging Face's LeRobot team for teams building with Mistral AI.
- **Two settings:** La Maison hosted the summit; Photoroom's offices hosted the build phase, according to the organizer's event listing.

> **Key idea:** The useful result of a robot hackathon is a demonstrated behavior with a clear account of what the team actually built.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Embodied AI:** Here, AI connects to a physical machine rather than producing only text; actions must result in observable behavior.
- **Software analogy:** Build a thin end-to-end feature: input request, model decision, robot action, and visible outcome, rather than several disconnected notebooks.
- **Worked planning exercise:** Sketch a single arm task, divide perception, control, and presentation work, and compare this plan with LeRobot Worldwide Hackathon submissions.

## How to engage

1. **Study the archive:** Watch Entrepreneurs First's event video, then read the published schedule to see how much time was reserved for building.
2. **Read team conditions:** The listing specified teams of five and individual acceptance; do not assume an entire association can register as one participant.
3. **Check future announcements:** This is a past event. Use the public host channel for later opportunities rather than assuming these equipment arrangements recur.

lessons.name: Physical AI Hackathon (Robotics Nation, Helsinki)
lessons.summary: Robotics Nation's Helsinki Physical AI Hackathon challenged teams to automate tasks using paired arms or an arm on a mobile base.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Robotics Nation's Helsinki Physical AI Hackathon challenged teams to automate tasks using paired arms or an arm on a mobile base.

![Two-arm cup-filling demonstration from the Helsinki hackathon project](/img/lessons/orgs_event_2-physical-ai-hackathon-robotics-nation-helsinki.webp)
*Two-arm cup-filling demonstration from the Helsinki hackathon project. Source: [Publisher](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NVHb-mLm7kE), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Two hardware tracks:** The listing offered two SO-101 arms working together, or an SO-101 on an omnidirectional LeKiwi platform with Jetson Orin Nano.
- **Short build cycle:** Teams of three to five had 48 hours; the event page lists a €5,000 prize pool and now shows registration closed.
- **Published example:** One team's repository documents two-arm tasks: filling a cup at a tap and placing an object into a cup.

> **Key idea:** Coordinating two arms means learning the relationship between their actions, not just making each arm move independently.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Software analogy:** Treat a two-arm task like cooperating services: one must place the cup where the other expects it before the next action makes sense.
- **Worked behavior:** In the published cup-filling demo, one arm brings the cup while the other operates the tap; both roles define success.
- **Connect the stack:** SO-101 and LeRobot turn the event into a concrete learning path rather than an abstract discussion of physical AI.

## How to engage

1. **Watch both task videos:** Identify the objects, each arm's role, and the visible completion condition before opening the implementation.
2. **Inspect the repository:** Follow its recorded training and deployment workflow; treat the team's reported experience as one project, not guaranteed performance.
3. **Contact public organizers:** Ask about future editions through the event page; do not travel based on the closed Helsinki listing.

lessons.name: RoboCup 2027 (Nuremberg)
lessons.summary: RoboCup 2027 is the robot competition announced for Nuremberg, where teams test autonomous systems in shared challenge environments.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

RoboCup 2027 is the robot competition announced for Nuremberg, where teams test autonomous systems in shared challenge environments.

![Official RoboCup 2027 logo for Nuremberg](/img/lessons/orgs_event_2-robocup-2027-nuremberg.webp)
*Official RoboCup 2027 logo for Nuremberg. Source: [Publisher](https://2027.robocup.org), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Announced venue and dates:** The organizer lists Messe Nürnberg and 15–21 June 2027 for the world championship.
- **More than football:** RoboCup's major categories include RoboCupSoccer, RoboCupRescue, RoboCup@Home, and Smart Manufacturing League.
- **Autonomous behavior:** In robot soccer, machines must perceive the game and act; the interesting engineering is not a human remotely choosing every move.

> **Key idea:** A league's rules define the engineering problem; choose the league before choosing the robot you want to build.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Software analogy:** A competition league resembles a shared test protocol: different teams implement systems that face comparable tasks and constraints.
- **Worked selection:** Compare a soccer task with an @Home service task; list the sensors, decisions, and physical actions each would require.
- **Local stepping stone:** RoboCup German Open is a separate event worth studying for match footage, results, and team preparation before considering the world championship.

## How to engage

1. **Watch the trailer:** Use it to understand the championship's scope, then read the major-league descriptions rather than assuming every league uses humanoids.
2. **Inspect qualification rules:** Follow the chosen league's current technical requirements and entry process; world-championship participation is not an automatic visitor registration.
3. **Plan a narrow contribution:** A perception benchmark, simulation tool, or reproducible subsystem may be a better first student deliverable than an entire competition team.

lessons.name: RoboCup German Open
lessons.summary: RoboCup German Open is a robot competition where university teams and younger competitors demonstrate autonomous systems in defined leagues.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

RoboCup German Open is a robot competition where university teams and younger competitors demonstrate autonomous systems in defined leagues.

![Robot competition scene published with the German Open 2026 archive](/img/lessons/orgs_event_2-robocup-german-open.webp)
*Robot competition scene published with the German Open 2026 archive. Source: [Publisher](https://robocup.de/germanopen-2026), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **2026 example:** The archived edition ran on 10–14 March at Messe Köln alongside the didacta education fair.
- **Different tasks:** The visitor guide lists home assistance, rescue, humanoid soccer, small-size soccer, and smart manufacturing among the major leagues.
- **Major versus Junior:** Major leagues serve research and university teams; Junior competitions provide a separate route for younger participants.

> **Key idea:** Choose one league and study its failures; a robot competition is a collection of different engineering problems, not one universal robot test.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Software analogy:** League rules act like a test specification, while a recorded match is a system trace showing decisions under real constraints.
- **Worked analysis:** Watch five minutes of one 2026 match; mark every visible perception, planning, and action failure, without assuming you know the underlying code.
- **Prepare for the larger event:** RoboCup 2027 (Nuremberg) is the world championship, not simply another name for this German Open archive.

## How to engage

1. **Start with footage:** Pair the Day 3 recording with the visitor guide to identify which league you are actually watching.
2. **Follow results to teams:** Use the official results page to find an entry worth investigating, then look for that team's public technical materials.
3. **Check future arrangements:** The current site separately announces a March 2027 German Junior final and June world championship in Nuremberg; do not reuse Cologne's schedule.

lessons.name: Robotex International
lessons.summary: Robotex International is an Estonia-rooted robotics festival with competitions for participants at different experience levels.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Robotex International is an Estonia-rooted robotics festival with competitions for participants at different experience levels.

![Published preview of Robotex International 2025](/img/lessons/orgs_event_2-robotex-international.webp)
*Published preview of Robotex International 2025. Source: [Publisher](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MT36qOQLj6U), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Autonomous tasks:** The competition directory describes line following, maze solving, sumo, and other challenges rather than one required robot design.
- **Simple starting point:** A line-following robot drives along a black marked track as quickly as possible; the rules make the physical objective visible.
- **More demanding variant:** Enhanced line following adds obstacles, inclines, and gaps, so completing a clean loop is no longer enough.

> **Key idea:** A small competition task can expose sensing and control problems without requiring an expensive general-purpose robot.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Software analogy:** Start with the smallest passing test, then introduce edge cases; a gap in the line is the physical equivalent of an unexpected input.
- **Worked progression:** Compare ordinary and enhanced line following; write a recovery rule for losing the line before optimizing speed on a perfect track.
- **Compare formats:** RoboCup German Open offers larger league systems; Robotex's task directory helps students explore more narrowly scoped challenge ideas.

## How to engage

1. **Watch a recent edition:** Use the 2025 aftermovie to see the setting, then the organizer's 2026 announcement for edition-specific context.
2. **Read the actual rules:** Choose one challenge and follow its linked rule document before selecting sensors or buying a chassis.
3. **Verify registration separately:** The directory mixes historical notices with rules; check current organizer announcements rather than treating an undated deadline as valid.

lessons.summary: Robotics & Automation at IntraLogisteX is a UK exhibition section about robots and automated systems used in warehouses and supply chains.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Robotics & Automation at IntraLogisteX is a UK exhibition section about robots and automated systems used in warehouses and supply chains.

![Exhibition scene from IntraLogisteX 2026](/img/lessons/orgs_event_2-robotics-automation-uk-with-intralogistex.webp)
*Exhibition scene from IntraLogisteX 2026. Source: [Publisher](https://www.roboticsandautomation.co.uk/), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Application focus:** Exhibits include robotic picking, mobile robots, goods-to-person systems, and automated storage and retrieval systems that put away and fetch stock.
- **More than hardware:** Warehouse software, sorting systems, and conferences connect individual machines with the operation around them.
- **Next announced edition:** The organizer lists 17–18 March 2027 at NEC Birmingham, with free exhibition entry and conference sessions.

> **Key idea:** For warehouse automation, the interesting unit is the complete material-flow process, not an isolated moving robot.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Software analogy:** Think of stock movements as transactions: a physical item changes place, and the surrounding software must maintain a meaningful account of that change.
- **Worked comparison:** Contrast a robot bringing stock to a person with an arm picking an item; list the inputs and completion signals each needs.
- **European comparison:** LogiMAT is another intralogistics-focused exhibition, useful for comparing how different suppliers describe the same warehouse problem.

## How to engage

1. **Begin with the recap:** Watch the official 2026 footage to identify a concrete application before browsing the current visitor information.
2. **Plan a technical question:** Ask an exhibitor how the demonstrated system receives a job and what it reports when the job cannot finish.
3. **Check access details:** Confirm the current registration conditions and program; a free visitor pass is not the same as permission to operate exhibited robots.

lessons.name: Robotics Summit & Expo
lessons.summary: Robotics Summit & Expo is a Boston conference and exhibition for developers building commercial robots and the technologies inside them.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Robotics Summit & Expo is a Boston conference and exhibition for developers building commercial robots and the technologies inside them.

![Attendees at Robotics Summit and Expo 2026](/img/lessons/orgs_event_2-robotics-summit-expo.webp)
*Attendees at Robotics Summit and Expo 2026. Source: [Publisher](https://www.roboticssummit.com/2026-recap/), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Developer audience:** The organizer names healthcare, logistics, manufacturing, aerospace, and defense among the markets represented.
- **Engineering plus exhibits:** Talks address enabling technology and development practices, while the exhibition lets visitors inspect components and complete systems.
- **2026 examples:** The featured-speaker list includes Dave Coleman of PickNik Robotics, Brian Gerkey of Intrinsic, and deployment engineers from robot companies.

> **Key idea:** A developer-focused exhibition is useful when you can connect a component or talk to a specific engineering problem.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Software analogy:** Treat it like a systems conference with a hardware dependency hall: the interfaces between parts can matter as much as their individual features.
- **Worked visit plan:** Pick one robot application and list the sensing, computing, motion, and integration questions you need answered before approaching a booth.
- **Compare with research:** Robotics: Science and Systems (RSS) 2027 emphasizes research papers; this summit emphasizes the engineering of robots intended for commercial use.

## How to engage

1. **Start remotely:** Compare the 2025 highlights with the 2026 introduction and official recap before deciding whether a Boston trip serves your project.
2. **Bring a reproducible problem:** A small repository, diagram of your setup, and precise question make a more useful conversation than asking what robotics is.
3. **Check the current program:** Do not assume every component exhibitor provides a beginner workshop, freely usable robot, or published implementation.

lessons.name: Robotics: Science and Systems (RSS) 2027
lessons.summary: Robotics: Science and Systems (RSS) 2027 is a robotics research conference announced for Athens on 6–11 July 2027.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Robotics: Science and Systems (RSS) 2027 is a robotics research conference announced for Athens on 6–11 July 2027.

![Official RSS 2026 Sydney artwork accompanying the archived recording](/img/lessons/orgs_event_2-robotics-science-and-systems-rss-2027.webp)
*Official RSS 2026 Sydney artwork accompanying the archived recording. Source: [Publisher](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pmi-4JFqZW0), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Research meeting:** RSS brings together robotics researchers for paper presentations, workshops, posters, and tutorials rather than a public robot-building tournament.
- **Single-track format:** Main presentations share one track, unlike a conference where many main sessions run simultaneously and attendees choose between them.
- **Current venue:** The official 2027 page identifies Megaron Athens International Conference Centre; use that information rather than assuming an earlier map location remains valid.

> **Key idea:** A research conference teaches you how to examine a contribution and its evidence, not merely collect impressive robot videos.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Software analogy:** Read a paper like a proposed optimization: what changed, what baseline was used, and which tests support the claimed improvement?
- **Worked reading exercise:** Choose one presentation from the 2026 recording; write three sentences describing its problem, method, and evidence before reading further.
- **Compare event purposes:** Robotics Summit & Expo is more commercially oriented; RSS is useful for finding research questions and understanding how results are reviewed.

## How to engage

1. **Start with an archive:** The linked video is from RSS 2026, not footage of the future Athens edition.
2. **Inspect the call:** The 2027 call describes a changed two-stage review process; read it before planning a student paper submission.
3. **Plan attendance separately:** Consult the official venue and future registration information; watching an archived talk does not require submitting research.

lessons.name: ROBOTWORLD
lessons.summary: ROBOTWORLD is a Korean exhibition covering industrial robots, service robots, mobile platforms, components, and related software.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

ROBOTWORLD is a Korean exhibition covering industrial robots, service robots, mobile platforms, components, and related software.

![Published preview of ROBOTWORLD 2026](/img/lessons/orgs_event_2-robotworld.webp)
*Published preview of ROBOTWORLD 2026. Source: [Publisher](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TFDLtkhu4oM), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **2026 setting:** The official introduction lists 4–7 November at KINTEX, Exhibition Hall 1, halls 3–5.
- **Broad exhibit range:** Categories include manufacturing and logistics robots, drones, smart manufacturing, and robot parts, not just humanoid machines.
- **Component example:** The organizer's exhibitor video on Samhyun focuses on smart actuators: devices that turn control commands into physical movement.

> **Key idea:** Look beneath a complete robot demonstration to identify the components and interfaces that make its behavior possible.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Software analogy:** A robot show resembles a software stack made tangible: an actuator is a dependency used by the higher-level application.
- **Worked comparison:** Watch the general event introduction, then the actuator exhibitor video; distinguish the robot's visible task from the parts enabling it.
- **Compare ecosystems:** iREX (International Robot Exhibition) offers a Japanese exhibition viewpoint, while ROBOTWORLD exposes another set of robot makers and component suppliers.

## How to engage

1. **Browse by application:** Start with logistics, manufacturing, or service robots in the introduction instead of trying to understand every booth at once.
2. **Prepare interface questions:** Ask which commands a component accepts, what feedback it returns, and which public documentation explains those interfaces.
3. **Use current notices:** The cited 2026 exhibition has ended. Follow official visitor and company information for subsequent editions rather than assuming identical dates or access.

lessons.name: ROSCon France
lessons.summary: ROSCon France is a French-speaking conference where robotics practitioners share experience with ROS, the open-source ecosystem for connecting robot software.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

ROSCon France is a French-speaking conference where robotics practitioners share experience with ROS, the open-source ecosystem for connecting robot software.

![ROSCon FR 2026 at Sorbonne University](/img/lessons/orgs_event_2-roscon-france.webp)
*ROSCon FR 2026 at Sorbonne University. Source: [Publisher](https://www.isir.upmc.fr/news/retour-sur-la-roscon-fr-2026-a-sorbonne-universite/), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Engineering community:** Sessions concern development tools, deployment, performance, research, and applications rather than one robot brand.
- **2026 format:** Sorbonne University hosted workshops and a hackathon on 22–23 June, then conference sessions on 24–25 June in Paris.
- **Concrete workshop:** The program included an introduction to ROS 2 and a session on ROS 2 Control with ODRI kits.

> **Key idea:** A ROS community meeting is a place to learn how other developers make separate robot software components work together.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Software analogy:** Think of ROS as plumbing between processes: developers need ways to exchange data and commands, not just a single large robot program.
- **Worked question:** The archived 2024 talk concerns computer vision on the robot's own computer; ask where its inputs originate and how results reach other components.
- **Use local expertise:** The Paris retrospective documents academic and industrial participants, making this a concrete French community to learn from rather than a distant brand.

## How to engage

1. **Start with a recording:** Watch the clearly labeled 2024 talk, then compare its topic with the 2026 program and retrospective.
2. **Join public discussion:** Use the French-speaking ROS community announcement to find official links and ask a precise, reproducible technical question.
3. **Check the next edition:** The 2026 page says registration is closed; do not treat its workshop listing as a current booking offer.

lessons.name: SIDO Lyon
lessons.summary: SIDO Lyon is a business technology event connecting robotics with AI, connected devices, and immersive technologies in industrial applications.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

SIDO Lyon is a business technology event connecting robotics with AI, connected devices, and immersive technologies in industrial applications.

![Published preview of SIDO Lyon 2026](/img/lessons/orgs_event_2-sido-lyon.webp)
*Published preview of SIDO Lyon 2026. Source: [Publisher](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=J9axawhUQm0), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Cross-technology focus:** The organizer brings together IoT, AI, robotics, and XR rather than treating robots as an isolated field.
- **Definitions:** IoT connects physical devices through networks; XR covers technologies that blend or simulate visual environments around a user.
- **Current announcement:** The site lists 15–16 September 2027 at Eurexpo Lyon and provides a retrospective of the 2026 edition.

> **Key idea:** A useful industrial demonstration explains how the robot, its data, and the business process fit together.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Software analogy:** Think of a connected factory demonstration as a full-stack application: a sensor measurement must connect meaningfully to software and an eventual action.
- **Worked booth exercise:** Sketch one demonstrated process as input, decision, action, and reported result; identify which part a 42AI team could realistically prototype.
- **Compare scopes:** Swiss Robotics Day centers the robotics ecosystem, while SIDO helps investigate the surrounding industrial and digital technologies.

## How to engage

1. **Start with the 2026 recap:** Identify a concrete application before browsing replay titles or considering an in-person visit.
2. **Choose one question:** For example, ask which data a robot sends to the monitoring software and what happens when that connection is unavailable.
3. **Check access conditions:** Use the organizer's current program and registration information; do not assume every exhibition includes hands-on student access or freely downloadable code.

lessons.name: START Hack
lessons.summary: START Hack is a student-led hackathon where mixed teams build prototypes for company-provided challenges, rather than a robotics-only contest.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

START Hack is a student-led hackathon where mixed teams build prototypes for company-provided challenges, rather than a robotics-only contest.

![Participants building at START Hack](/img/lessons/orgs_event_2-start-hack.webp)
*Participants building at START Hack. Source: [Publisher](https://www.startglobal.org/start-hack), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Flagship format:** The organizer describes a 36-hour build event in St. Gallen involving technical, design, and business participants.
- **Concrete constraints:** Teams work on industry cases, meaning a partner's specified problem rather than an unrestricted idea of their own.
- **Separate formats:** The site also lists START Hack League and local tour events; these should not be confused with the flagship hackathon.

> **Key idea:** Read the case before selecting a technology; a working answer to the brief matters more than forcing robotics into an unrelated challenge.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Software analogy:** Treat a company case like an issue with acceptance criteria: the team must show the requested behavior in a limited development window.
- **Worked preparation:** Take a published case and write a minimal demo plan with one input, one visible result, and one testable success criterion.
- **Pair complementary events:** START Summit is the related networking conference; LeRobot Worldwide Hackathon provides a more explicitly robot-focused building format.

## How to engage

1. **Watch earlier editions:** Compare the 2025 and 2026 aftermovies to understand team delivery before reading the current hacker information.
2. **Check current cases:** Only plan robot hardware if the actual brief and organizer conditions support it; the event does not promise a robotics track.
3. **Verify the edition:** The current flagship announcement lists 17–19 March 2027; local 24-hour tour notices describe different events.

lessons.name: START Summit
lessons.summary: START Summit is a St. Gallen startup conference connecting founders, investors, students, and technology organizations, not a robot-building competition.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

START Summit is a St. Gallen startup conference connecting founders, investors, students, and technology organizations, not a robot-building competition.

![Conference scene published on the START Summit website](/img/lessons/orgs_event_2-start-summit.webp)
*Conference scene published on the START Summit website. Source: [Publisher](https://www.startglobal.org/start-summit), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Meeting platform:** The event centers on the Alpine technology ecosystem and provides talks, meetings, pitching opportunities, and introductions.
- **Announced edition:** The official site lists 18–19 March 2027 in St. Gallen; its prominently displayed attendance figures describe the 2026 edition.
- **Different from START Hack:** The related hackathon is the building sprint; the summit is the place to discuss projects and potential collaborations.

> **Key idea:** A networking conference becomes useful when you arrive with a demonstrated project and a specific reason to meet someone.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Software analogy:** Treat your project introduction like a README: explain the problem, show what runs, identify limitations, and give a clear next step.
- **Worked preparation:** Prepare a one-minute robot demo, one sentence describing its user, and one concrete request such as feedback on the deployment problem.
- **Keep the fit honest:** Robotics is one possible project topic here, not a guaranteed track; Swiss Robotics Day provides a more explicitly robotics-centered meeting environment.

## How to engage

1. **Browse past editions:** Use the 2025 and 2026 official recaps to understand the audience before committing student travel funds.
2. **Read admission information:** Check the FAQ and current ticket categories; do not assume a START Hack application automatically includes every summit activity.
3. **Follow through:** After a relevant conversation, send the promised repository or demonstration with a precise question rather than a general request for sponsorship.

lessons.name: Swiss Robotics Day
lessons.summary: Swiss Robotics Day is a Zurich event bringing robotics researchers, companies, students, and other participants together around talks and exhibited systems.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

Swiss Robotics Day is a Zurich event bringing robotics researchers, companies, students, and other participants together around talks and exhibited systems.

![Published preview of Swiss Robotics Day 2025](/img/lessons/orgs_event_2-swiss-robotics-day.webp)
*Published preview of Swiss Robotics Day 2025. Source: [Publisher](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EE5-Fxnl4UU), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **2026 setting:** The organizer reports 1,404 visitors from 35 countries at StageOne Zurich on 13 November.
- **Robotics ecosystem:** The published floor list includes university laboratories, component companies, robot makers, and startups rather than one competition league.
- **Concrete examples:** Listed exhibitors include EPFL Xplore, ETH Zurich's Robotic Systems Lab, maxon, and multiple industrial robot suppliers.

> **Key idea:** An ecosystem event is most valuable when you can connect a laboratory, component supplier, or robot company to a specific project need.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Software analogy:** Treat the exhibitor list like a dependency map: some organizations provide complete systems, others supply a component or a piece of expertise.
- **Worked visit plan:** Choose one lab, one component maker, and one robot company; prepare a different technical question for each rather than repeating a generic pitch.
- **Compare formats:** Robotics and AI hackathons emphasize building under time pressure; Swiss Robotics Day emphasizes demonstrations, technical exchange, and meeting the surrounding community.

## How to engage

1. **Start with archived footage:** Watch the 2025 highlights to identify the exhibition format, then the 2026 teaser for that edition's context.
2. **Sample a technical session:** The archived Davide Scaramuzza talk shows how a substantial research presentation differs from an event overview.
3. **Follow official updates:** The site says 2027 is in preparation; do not assume a new date or registration process from the completed 2026 edition.

lessons.name: TUM.ai Makeathon
lessons.summary: TUM.ai Makeathon is the signature hackathon of Munich's TUM.ai student initiative, focused on team-built AI prototypes rather than exclusively on robots.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

TUM.ai Makeathon is the signature hackathon of Munich's TUM.ai student initiative, focused on team-built AI prototypes rather than exclusively on robots.

![Published preview of the TUM.ai Makeathon 2023](/img/lessons/orgs_event_2-tum-ai-makeathon.webp)
*Published preview of the TUM.ai Makeathon 2023. Source: [Publisher](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zgDPAU71Jgw), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Student organizer:** TUM.ai describes itself as a nonprofit initiative at the Technical University of Munich connecting AI research with practical projects.
- **Documented format:** Public Makeathon materials include an event aftermovie and a recorded final with project presentations and awards.
- **Wider event program:** The current archive lists partner hackathons, talks, and a November 2024 BenchPress Makeathon; these are distinct editions and formats.

> **Key idea:** Use an AI hackathon to practice producing and explaining a working prototype; confirm the actual challenge before assuming it involves robot hardware.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Software analogy:** A Makeathon demo resembles a small release: it needs an executable path from input to useful output, not a collection of disconnected experiments.
- **Worked preparation:** Watch one team's final presentation and summarize its problem, input data, output, and demonstrated limitation.
- **Choose a robotics fit:** LeRobot Worldwide Hackathon is explicitly robot-focused; use that contrast when deciding whether a TUM.ai case suits your lab's current project.

## How to engage

1. **Start with an archive:** The linked aftermovie is from 2023 and the final from 2021, not advertisements for an unverified future Makeathon.
2. **Read current cases:** Use the organizer's event archive and public updates to check dates, team requirements, and whether a new event is actually announced.
3. **Scope your contribution:** Offer a reproducible software prototype or clearly explained demonstration; do not assume the organizer provides robots, sensors, or workshop equipment.

lessons.summary: VivaTech is a Paris technology and startup event where robotics demonstrations appear within a much broader innovation and business program.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

VivaTech is a Paris technology and startup event where robotics demonstrations appear within a much broader innovation and business program.

![Panel discussion at VivaTech 2026](/img/lessons/orgs_event_2-vivatech.webp)
*Panel discussion at VivaTech 2026. Source: [Publisher](https://vivatech.com/news/viva-tech-2026-day-one-digest), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Broad audience:** The organizer addresses startups, established companies, investors, media, and other visitors rather than only robotics researchers.
- **Robotics example:** Its 2026 program included La Grande Parade des Robots Humanoïdes, a session devoted to humanoid robots.
- **Current announcement:** The official site lists 16–19 June 2027 at Paris Expo Porte de Versailles; archived 2026 footage describes the previous edition.

> **Key idea:** Use a broad technology show to discover applications and contacts, then verify robot capabilities through technical evidence beyond the stage demonstration.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Humanoid:** A robot with a broadly human-like body is one robot form, not a guarantee of human-level reasoning or general-purpose capability.
- **Software analogy:** A stage demo is like a product launch, not a test report; you still need the implementation constraints and repeatable examples.
- **Worked visit exercise:** Choose one observed robot task and list what is visibly demonstrated, what the presenter claims, and what remains untested.

## How to engage

1. **Watch a specific recap:** Start with Associated Press's 2026 exhibit report, then compare it with VivaTech's own event coverage.
2. **Prepare a focused introduction:** Bring a short working demo and explain which user problem your 42AI team is investigating before approaching an exhibitor.
3. **Check access and scope:** Read current ticket and program information; a public humanoid parade is not the same as a robot-learning workshop.

lessons.name: World Artificial Intelligence Conference (WAIC)
lessons.summary: WAIC is a Shanghai conference and exhibition about artificial intelligence, including robot applications alongside models, computing infrastructure, and governance.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

WAIC is a Shanghai conference and exhibition about artificial intelligence, including robot applications alongside models, computing infrastructure, and governance.

![Pudu Robotics' demonstration at WAIC 2026](/img/lessons/orgs_event_2-world-artificial-intelligence-conference-waic.webp)
*Pudu Robotics' demonstration at WAIC 2026. Source: [Publisher](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=anlqsvM-6_0), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **2026 setting:** Official and on-site reporting place the World Artificial Intelligence Conference on 17–20 July in Shanghai.
- **Physical applications:** Jiemian's exhibition report describes robots moving beyond software demonstrations into workplaces, factories, and pharmacies.
- **One exhibitor viewpoint:** Pudu Robotics' event video presents its own physical-AI demonstrations; it is a vendor's selected showcase, not a neutral benchmark.

> **Key idea:** Distinguish the robot's demonstrated task from the wider AI narrative surrounding it.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Physical AI:** This means applying AI to machines acting in the physical world, where movement and interaction matter as well as model output.
- **Software analogy:** A model is one service inside a larger deployed system; a robot also needs meaningful connections between sensing, decisions, and physical action.
- **Worked comparison:** Contrast the Pudu showcase with Jiemian's floor report; record the task, visible inputs, output action, and missing performance evidence for one robot.

## How to engage

1. **Start with reporting:** Use the two videos to understand the event, then read the on-site article for context on the exhibited applications.
2. **Investigate one system:** Follow the named exhibitor's technical materials rather than treating conference-wide attendance or product totals as evidence of robot capability.
3. **Compare events:** World Robot Conference (WRC) is more specifically robot-centered; WAIC places robots within a broader AI and computing conversation.

lessons.name: World FIRA
lessons.summary: World FIRA is an agricultural robotics event where manufacturers, farmers, researchers, and other participants examine robots working in real field conditions.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

World FIRA is an agricultural robotics event where manufacturers, farmers, researchers, and other participants examine robots working in real field conditions.

![Published preview of the World FIRA 2025 field demonstrations](/img/lessons/orgs_event_2-world-fira.webp)
*Published preview of the World FIRA 2025 field demonstrations. Source: [Publisher](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LAFk4mT5faY), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Agricultural setting:** The official site combines field demonstrations, robot information sheets, expert discussions, and a scientific workshop.
- **Concrete archive:** The 2025 material documents demonstrations near Toulouse on 4–6 February; the robot directory explicitly labels its entries as 2025 solutions.
- **Many crop contexts:** The directory lets visitors filter by crops such as vineyards, berries, vegetables, and field crops rather than treating every farm alike.

> **Key idea:** A farm robot's usefulness depends on the task, crop, and operating conditions, not just whether it can drive across a field.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Software analogy:** A crop and terrain combination is an execution environment: the same algorithm may behave differently when its assumptions about inputs change.
- **Worked comparison:** Choose two robots from different crop filters; record the intended crop, demonstrated operation, and which environmental conditions the public material actually explains.
- **Compare application depth:** LogiMAT focuses on indoor material flow; World FIRA helps students investigate how robotics problems change in agricultural settings.

## How to engage

1. **Watch real field footage:** Begin with the official 2025 aftermovie, then inspect a specific robot's information sheet rather than general promotional claims.
2. **Prepare a farmer-facing question:** Ask which task is automated, what still needs an operator, and how the demonstration relates to everyday field use.
3. **Check the current format:** The site also promotes GOFAR tour activities; verify the exact event before using the archived Toulouse dates to plan attendance.

lessons.name: World Robot Conference (WRC)
lessons.summary: World Robot Conference is a Beijing event combining robotics discussions, an exhibition, and competitions across several robot application areas.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

World Robot Conference is a Beijing event combining robotics discussions, an exhibition, and competitions across several robot application areas.

![Scene published by the World Robot Conference organizers](/img/lessons/orgs_event_2-world-robot-conference-wrc.webp)
*Scene published by the World Robot Conference organizers. Source: [Publisher](https://www.worldrobotconference.com/), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Different event parts:** The official site separates the conference, robot expo, and contest activities; they do not all test the same abilities.
- **Exhibition range:** Its 2026 expo describes humanoids, industrial robots, service robots, specialized robots, and core components from companies and research institutions.
- **Visible examples:** Associated Press footage and the 2026 photo report show humanoids performing tasks alongside other exhibited machines.

> **Key idea:** An exhibition shows selected behaviors; a capability claim needs conditions, repeatable trials, and evidence beyond a striking demonstration.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Software analogy:** Treat a stage performance like a curated application demo, not a passing result on every test case your project might encounter.
- **Worked viewing exercise:** Pick one filmed task; write what you can actually observe, what is hidden, and one repeatable test you would request.
- **Compare event scope:** World Artificial Intelligence Conference (WAIC) covers the broader AI ecosystem, while WRC centers robots, their components, applications, and related competitions.

## How to engage

1. **Start with independent coverage:** Watch the Associated Press footage before browsing the organizer's expo descriptions and named exhibits.
2. **Follow a specific application:** Investigate one robot's published technical documentation rather than using a conference-wide publicity figure as a measure of technical maturity.
3. **Read figures carefully:** The official homepage labels several totals as cumulative across editions; do not mistake them for attendance at the 2026 event.

lessons.name: WorldSkills France
lessons.summary: WorldSkills France organizes practical skills competitions, including mobile robotics and industrial robot integration, with regional, national, and international pathways.
lessons.lesson_md:
## In one sentence

WorldSkills France organizes practical skills competitions, including mobile robotics and industrial robot integration, with regional, national, and international pathways.

![Mobile robotics competition setup published by WorldSkills France](/img/lessons/orgs_event_2-worldskills-france.webp)
*Mobile robotics competition setup published by WorldSkills France. Source: [Publisher](https://www.worldskills-france.org/metiers/robotique/), license unknown.*

## What they do in robotics

- **Mobile robotics:** Competitors work with machines that perceive, decide, and act to carry out tasks autonomously, rather than following continuous human control.
- **Robot integration:** This means making a robot arm, its tools, programming, communications, and industrial process work together for applications such as sorting or welding.
- **Two distinct disciplines:** The official métier pages describe different skills; do not assume mobile robotics and industrial arm integration use the same equipment or assessment.

> **Key idea:** Robotics skill means delivering a working system against a brief, not merely writing a program that compiles.

## Why they matter for 42AI

- **Software analogy:** Integration resembles end-to-end testing: separate components may each work while the full process still fails its acceptance criteria.
- **Worked exercise:** Choose a sorting process from the integration page and list the object input, sensing decision, arm action, and successful final placement.
- **Compare competitions:** KUKA Innovation Award emphasizes a research application; WorldSkills France emphasizes practical competence within defined occupational disciplines.

## How to engage

1. **Start visually:** Watch the official mobile-robotics competition video, then compare the two discipline descriptions to identify the skills you lack.
2. **Check eligibility by discipline:** The participation page says age limits depend on the métier; do not assume that every 42 student qualifies.
3. **Use the regional route:** WorldSkills France says participation is free and registration begins through the appropriate region; read current conditions before planning an entry.
